utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: We'll see if they can get it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: Make it work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: I hope that they can make it work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: Even if it does, let's keep in mind that housing delayed is housing denied.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: We are seeing another developer start over and people unable to move in for another couple of years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: And it strikes me that for the most part, this wasn't a policy disagreement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: Just about everyone involved wanted as much affordable housing as possible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: Some people thought we could get 100% affordable building, and that's what they were advocating for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: Others, like myself, said the funds for that didn't exist.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: We would need to go with some sort of balance or some other sort of balance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: Some people were wondering, do we have the infrastructure, the plumbing, the schools, et cetera, to support more than a certain number of new residents?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: All of these were technical questions, economic questions, not policy questions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: The question was, how do we get as much affordable housing as possible built?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: And from everything I've heard this afternoon, from everything I've learned about him by reading about him, I think Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: Mangin is an excellent choice for this sort of technical economic role, which is exactly what he's been nominated for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: I will also say that I like most of what I heard from him about policy, but the policy continues to come from this council, who make sure that we're fighting for affordable housing, for development wherever it's appropriate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: City of Yes being a great example.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: The council continues to engage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: Thomas, sorry, sorry, apologies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: I encourage you to confirm.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey Thomas
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Janes
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the next panelists to unmute themselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Janes
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Jack, a Ridgewood resident, points to Mangin's 2018 paper 'Ethnic Enclaves and the Zoning Game' as demonstrating his familiarity with local constituencies and nuanced relationships to land use policy, which he says should allay concerns about his commitment to local control.
chapters.title: Public (Zoom): Jack supports Mangin, citing 2018 paper on ethnic enclaves

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jack
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jack
utterances.text: My name is Jack.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jack
utterances.text: I'm a resident of Ridgewood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jack
utterances.text: And I would echo the points made by other community members about John Mangin's competence and qualifications.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jack
utterances.text: And Dan's point about the importance of balancing local control with the need, the urgent need to build housing for the entire city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jack
utterances.text: That said, I think that in a housing crisis that is rapidly escalating, I think we really need someone that does have the granular situational local awareness that John Manchin does have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jack
utterances.text: Council members have referred to Manchin's 2014 paper, The New Exclusionary Zoning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jack
utterances.text: But I would point to a different 2018 paper of his called Ethnic Enclaves and the Zoning Game

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jack
utterances.text: that really demonstrates his intimate familiarity and interest in many different local constituencies and their unique nuanced relationships to land use policy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jack
utterances.text: I think it goes...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jack
utterances.text: I think it goes a lot to allay the concerns that many council members have had about John Manchin's priority with local control.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jack
utterances.text: John understands the need to build 700,000 units of good

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jack
utterances.text: affordable housing in the next 10 years, and I urge the City Council to confirm him.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jack
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Can the next panelist go?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Gray
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Are there other panelists on the Zoom panel?

chapters.summary: Mehta, NY Director at RPA, strongly supports Mangin, noting the BSA's expanded fast-track authority makes this appointment critical. He praises Mangin's decade of public service at DCP, his thoughtfulness, and his commitment to responsible governance, and urges confirmation.
chapters.title: Public (Zoom): Maulin Mehta (Regional Plan Association) supports Mangin

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms.

utterances.text: Lameda.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Oon, Deputy Speaker Williams, and members of the committee for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta

utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: We are all aware of how critical our city's housing crisis is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: For years, RPA has been sounding the alarm that we simply do not have enough homes to meet the needs of current and future New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: We need an all-of-the-above approach to build more housing in more places of all types and affordability levels.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: To do so, we need to reform regulations that have too often made good projects difficult to deliver.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: That's why the work of the BSA is so important today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: New Yorkers approved a new process last year that would enable the BSA to provide a faster path for certain types of affordable housing development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: Along with many of our fellow advocates, RPA supported the fundamental goal of that reform, to make it easier to advance affordable housing projects while still maintaining a transparent public process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: The success of that reform will now depend on how well it's implemented.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: BSA leadership with sound judgment, deep understanding of how housing gets built, and commitment to fairness and consistency is critical to building trust and success.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: John Mangin clearly brings those qualities to the position.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: He has dedicated over a decade of public service at DCP, where he's worked on some of the most consequential housing reforms the city has undertaken while leading their housing division.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: In our housing research and advocacy efforts, we have worked very closely with John over the years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: He is a thoughtful and knowledgeable public servant dedicated to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: responsible governance to solve our housing challenges.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: The BSA must be a credible, independent institution that can review land use questions and make decisions fairly, responsibly, and predictably with transparency and accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: John has dedicated his career serving the city, and we believe he is particularly well qualified to lead the BSA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: We know he will work closely with the City Council and be responsive to community feedback as we all work collectively to solve our housing challenges.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maulin Mehta
utterances.text: We urge you to confirm his nomination.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Janes
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Janes
utterances.text: Your time expired.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the next panelists on the Zoom panel to unmute themselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Janes
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Handler, a Queens resident, testifies in support, noting the 1.4% vacancy rate is the lowest since 1968 and the city needs 700,000 additional homes. He says Mangin's willingness to speak honestly about where the zoning system has fallen short is a qualification, not a disqualification.
chapters.title: Public (Zoom): Peter Handler supports Mangin, citing vacancy crisis

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Handler
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Handler
utterances.text: My name is Peter Handler.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Handler
utterances.text: I'm a resident of Queens, and I'm here to testify in support of John Magan's nomination to chair the Board of Standards and Appeals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Handler
utterances.text: In my own work, I've seen what the housing crisis means for people with very limited resources and very few alternatives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Handler
utterances.text: So to me, this is not an abstract debate about zoning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Handler
utterances.text: When there simply are not enough affordable homes, the most vulnerable New Yorkers suffer the most.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Handler
utterances.text: We know the scale of the problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Handler
utterances.text: The citywide vacancy rate is just 1.4%, the lowest since 1968, and HPD estimates that the city will need about 700,000 additional homes over the next decade.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Handler
utterances.text: John Mangan has spent more than a decade working on these issues at the Department of City Planning, including City of Yes and mandatory inclusionary zoning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Handler
utterances.text: With the BSA now responsible for considering applications to expedite publicly financed 100% affordable housing, that experience matters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Handler
utterances.text: And frankly, his willingness to speak honestly about where our zoning and land use system has fallen, strikes, has fallen short, strikes me as a qualification, not a disqualification.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Handler
utterances.text: I urge the council to confirm John Mangan as BSA chair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Handler
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Is there any other panelists on Zoom right now?

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Can the last person on the Zoom panel unmute themselves?

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Zimmerman, a lower Manhattan resident, supports Mangin, noting the BSA chair will determine whether the city carries out the voter-approved fast-track mandate or continues to let affordable housing die in process. He says 'housing delayed is housing denied' and urges confirmation without delay.
chapters.title: Public (Zoom): Sam Zimmerman supports Mangin, urging confirmation without delay

utterances.text: Sorry, is this me?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman
utterances.text: Am I unmuted?

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman
utterances.text: Hi.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman
utterances.text: Good afternoon, chair members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman
utterances.text: My name is Sam Zimmerman, and I'm testifying today in support of John Mangin's nomination to chair the Board of Standards and Appeals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman
utterances.text: I am a resident of lower Manhattan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman
utterances.text: And John has served our city for more than a decade, where he led, among other things, City of Yes for Housing Opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman
utterances.text: He served as Director of Policy and Research for the 2025 Charter Revision Commission, which produced the most significant changes to the city's land use review process in decades.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman
utterances.text: Very few people in New York understand both the mechanics of zoning and the human stakes of housing scarcity as well as he does.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman
utterances.text: New York City's residents recognize we're in a housing crisis and overwhelmingly approved the affordable housing fast track last year, giving BSA the power to approve certain 100% affordable projects on an expedited timeline.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman
utterances.text: That means...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman
utterances.text: The person chairing the board will determine directly whether the city rises to the moment and carries out the mandate granted by voters, or if it continues to allow affordable housing to die in process, as we've done for decades.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman
utterances.text: We need someone who understands both the legal terrain and the urgency of this moment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman
utterances.text: John Manchin is that person.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman
utterances.text: Housing delayed is housing denied, and I urge this committee and the full council to confirm John Manchin without delay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sam Zimmerman
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: And now we are moving back to in-person panels.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: So again, what I

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: For your name, please come up.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: And when you finish speaking, the next panelist could start speaking.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: First, we have Christopher Leon Johnson.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: We have Howard Slackin.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: We have Joshua Robles.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: And we have Revlon O'Connor.

chapters.summary: Johnson supports the nomination 100% but complains that Zoom panelists were allowed to speak before in-person speakers, contrary to the expected order. He criticizes the council speaker for opposing the nomination after voting for City of Yes, and accuses security of lying about a former council member being present.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Yeah, my name is Christopher Leon Johnson.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: I didn't like how that was handled, okay?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: I support the nomination 100%, but look, if y'all want support, y'all shouldn't be treating people like that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: And some of you guys actually support the city, yes, like the one next to you, Mrs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson

chapters.summary: Robles testifies in support, arguing the housing crisis is driven by distrust and that Mangin can repair trust by building housing that fits neighborhoods and is approved by local residents, creating harmony between advocates and skeptics.
chapters.title: Public: Joshua Robles supports Mangin, emphasizing trust-building

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: My name is Josh.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: I am here to testify in support of John Mangion, and it is an honor to be here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: We cannot ignore that our housing crisis is largely driven by distrust.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: Distrust of residents who feel suspicious about new developments in their neighborhoods.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: They have every right to feel how they want to feel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: To me, however, John Manchin not only has the chance to make life better for all of us, but to repair trust that will go far in making both a more harmonious and affordable city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: I want John Manchin to fast-track affordable housing for the same economic and social reasons that others have mentioned here before me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: But in addition to that, I also do want and he wants housing that does fit the neighborhood and is approved by people in the neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: I truly believe that building housing that looks like I could fix its neighborhood and was approved by and involved people in the neighborhood not only builds housing, but builds trust.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: Builds trust between those who advocate and those who are more skeptical.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: Listening to others, listening to those who disagree, encourages them to listen to those who want a more equitable society.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: Rebuilding trust between different parts of society is a virtue, and I think John Manchin will do that, and we can make a more affordable city in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: O'Connor, pastor of First Presbyterian Church in Jamaica, supports Mangin based on his experience with the Jamaica Neighborhood Rezoning. He says Mangin listened to multiple community perspectives and brought critical tools for affordable housing at the volume needed to respond to displacement in Southeast Queens.
chapters.title: Public: Rev. Patrick O'Connor supports Mangin based on Jamaica rezoning experience

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: Good afternoon, I'm Reverend Patrick O'Connor, pastor of First Presbyterian Church in Jamaica and a leader with Metro Industrial Areas Foundation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: We organize for thousands of units of affordable housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: My congregation and the neighborhood of Southeast Queens

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: has lost many families because there's not enough affordable housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: I am here to testify in support of John Mangian as chair of the Board of Standards and Appeals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: Last year, I actively participated in the Jamaican neighborhood rezoning

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: Incredibly led by Deputy Speaker Nantasha Williams and approved by the City Council, it was my experience that Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: Mangin and other DCP staff listened and were responsive to multiple interests and perspectives of community residents, landowners,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: for-profits, non-profits, different economic and racial groups.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: He brought the critical tools needed to produce

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: use housing at the volume and scale needed to respond to the neglect and overpricing that has pushed out many residents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: Confirming him will ensure that New York City has an experienced, knowledgeable, skilled,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: and capable leader who can respond to the council's objectives, the mayor's housing agenda,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: and ultimately the hundreds of thousands of families who in this housing emergency have no place to go.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: The council should

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: support and vote for John Mangian as the new BSA chair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Patrick O'Connor
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: And we're going to go back on Zoom right now.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: I could ask the people, the panelists on Zoom, I'm going to call on former Councilman Garanek to unmute themselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Robles
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Garodnick, former council member and DCP director, joins the hearing to rebut earlier attacks on Mangin's character. He calls Mangin smart, dedicated, honest, and direct, and says the BSA's narrow legal focus is well-suited to someone who understands the law and council prerogatives. He urges confirmation.
chapters.title: Public (Zoom): Former DCP Chair Dan Garodnick strongly supports Mangin

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: Hello there, Madam Chair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: Wonderful.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: Well, my name is Dan Garodnik.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: Good to see you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: As you know, I served for 12 years as a member of the council and over the past four years as the director of the Department of City Planning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: I'm here today to strongly support the nomination of John Mangin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: I was just going to submit my testimony by paper, which of course I did, but I was listening to the hearing online and I heard a presenter on an earlier panel take direct aim at

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: John Mangin's character, his temperament, his honesty, his suitability to serve in any level of government.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: And with that, I wanted to join the hearing myself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: Those sorts of attacks are totally unacceptable, particularly for someone who has distinguished himself as a smart, dedicated, and yes, honest and direct public servant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: You know, you see a lot of what happened at the hearings today was taking small bits of pieces of words that John has written in Larview articles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: And yes, he is an academic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: And yes, he is a booster of more housing, more housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: types of housing at all levels and all corners of the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: But what should not get lost here is that he is as qualified and excellent a candidate as one might find for this role.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: He is a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: He has integrity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: As you all know, the BSA has a very specific and narrow focus.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: For that, I am certain he will follow the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: He has already said today he will have an open door to the council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: I have seen that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: He has the patience to be able to digest complicated thoughts and to bring them into reality and to listen to community concerns.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: He will be an excellent choice, and I certainly hope that you, Madam Chair, and your colleagues will confirm him.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: Thank you for hearing me out.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: I believe Councilman Romano has a question.

chapters.summary: Morano asks Garodnick to put his council member hat on and address concerns about Mangin's skepticism of local influence. Garodnick confirms council members know their communities best and that must be balanced with citywide housing needs, saying Mangin understands both. He shares that Mangin always took community concerns seriously during their four years working together.
chapters.title: CM Morano questions Garodnick on member deference and local knowledge

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And thank you, Citizen Garadnik.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It's been a while since you've had that title.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It's great to hear from you.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I think your perspective is particularly valuable here because you've sat on both sides of this.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: You served in this body representing a district dealing with land use issues and then obviously your role at city planning, which you alluded to.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Let me...

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Ask you to put your council member hat back on for a minute because you know I've never been shy about asking your advice about how to be a good council member.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: One of the concerns that I have about John Mangan is in his intelligence or his knowledge of land use or his integrity, which you cited.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Those are pretty obvious.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It's a philosophy that seems skeptical at times of how much influence

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: local communities and their elected representatives should have over development.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: When you were sitting where we're sitting, did you ever think that member deference and neighborhood opposition served a legitimate purpose?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And are there cases where you think a local council member actually does know something about his or her district a bit more than the planners downtown?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: I love that question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: It's good to see you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: The short answer is yes, of course, Councilmembers know their communities the best, and they advocate for their communities, and they want to make sure that they're delivering the right outcome for their communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: It is equally true that New York City is facing a historic housing crisis with a 1.4% vacancy rate in housing, something that is as low as it has been since 1968.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: And we need to find some citywide solutions and find ways to deal with this, which is why the City Council deserves so much credit for having taken big steps in the last few years to advance citywide housing initiatives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: But you're really asking me to put my council member hat on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: The short answer is yes, local council members have a significant role, need to make sure that the voices of their communities are heard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: And that needs to be balanced with the citywide needs for the crisis that we're in, the moment that we're in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: And I believe to the nominee who is before you, he gets it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: He understands that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: You know he's a booster of housing supply.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: That's not a secret.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: He understands that we need to actually turn the ship around in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: In order to reduce costs, make sure that tenants have rights in New York, to reduce pressures of gentrification, displacement, really take the burdens off of some of the neighborhoods that really have struggled for a very long time

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: with doing the work for most of the rest of the city, which has not seen much housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: He understands all of that, but importantly at the BSA, he also knows how to follow the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: He knows how to look at the facts, the circumstances, the very specific findings that will be present before him.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: And he, I heard him say earlier in this hearing a number of times that he will have an open door to members of the council to hear them out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: And I believe that if I were in your shoes, I would look at a candidate like that and I would say, hey, BSA has a very narrow, very legal focus.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: They have the ability to evaluate very specific opportunities in a very narrow scope.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: This is a guy who understands the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: He understands the boundaries of what he can and cannot do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: And he also understands the council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: I know he understands the council because I worked with him for four years directly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: We talked about the city council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: You might not be surprised to know a lot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: And I made sure that, you know, we were working together to find ways to respect city council prerogatives, to respect the city council, to make sure we were hearing, understanding, and delivering in those areas where we could.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: So I think you have a great candidate, and I would view him that way if I were sitting in your seat today, Councilman.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: In that time,

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: You got that ringside seat for that kind of work.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Have you ever seen Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Mangin take seriously a community's objection to development and conclude, you know what, they're right, this shouldn't be built or this proposal needs to be scaled back?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: You know, John was not necessarily in every conversation that I had about housing proposals or specific development sites throughout the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: He was the one who was thinking about bigger, broader housing policies for the agency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: But when he was brought in to talk about specific issues or needs or concerns, the issues of community, community interests and needs were always there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: He always took them seriously.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Garodnick
utterances.text: And we all worked together to try to find ways in which we could address the issues that actually could be addressed.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Now I'm moving back to in-person panelists.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: I'm going to call up Brad Greenberg and Ariel Hirsch.

chapters.summary: Greenberg, executive director of the NYU Furman Center, contextualizes Mangin's 2014 article within decades of academic research including Rothstein's 'Color of Law' and Fischel's work on home voters. He notes BSA's governance has many checks and balances and that the council retains significant power over its structure.
chapters.title: Public: Brad Greenberg (NYU Furman Center) contextualizes Mangin's academic writing

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: Hello, Council Members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: I'm Brad Greenberg.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: I'm the Executive Director of the NYU Furman Center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: The NYU Furman Center is a joint academic research center of the NYU School of Law and the Robert F.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: Wagner Graduate School of Public Service.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: We're an organization committed to leveraging rigorous evidence-based research on housing and urban development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: And we're here today to talk and contextualize some of what's been discussed in the academic literature.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: A couple things I want to say first about the Board of Standard and Appeals and the role it plays in New York City's land use process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: Unlike DCP, or City Planning Commission, they don't take as active a role in land use policy, including initiating changes to planning policy and ushering items through the Euler process, but they do determine

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: individual applications and approve and deny special permits and variances, which you've heard about today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: So the BSA's role is really a highly structured, cabined process focused on reviewing individual applications, and it requires someone with a lot of technical expertise in the case law and regulations governing land use in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: So the council should be very focused on the nominee's expertise in this highly technical area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: The other thing I'll say about the Board of Standards and Appeals is the structure and governance has a lot of checks and balances in the process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: So there are five members appointed for a six-year term.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: The mayor appoints one member as the chair, but everything is done by a majority vote, even though the chair oversees public hearings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: They also impose in the statute governing the Board of Standards and Appeals a lot of transparency requirements, including obligations to go through a community board process, as well as solicit council input on individual applications.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: And the council has previously in 2017 also changed the governance of the BSA and retains a decent amount of power over how it's structured.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: So that's important to remember.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: There's a lot of checks and balances in the BSA itself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: I do also want to say one thing about Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: Mangin's 2014 publication, which I know has come up a lot today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: Obviously, we're one of the leading academic research centers on housing policy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: I just want to say that the article itself does build on many decades of work and research, including Richard Rothstein's book, The Color of Law, and Bill Fischel's book, and previous books on home voters and the economics of land use.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: And it's absolutely within the scope of the academic literature.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: I'm sure there are words everyone would take back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: Sorry, please wrap it up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to say about the academic work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brad Greenberg
utterances.text: Thanks.

chapters.summary: Hirsch, UHAB policy director, supports Mangin and brings a guidebook he helped create at the Center for Urban Pedagogy explaining affordable housing, zoning, and ULURP at an eighth-grade level. She says his technical knowledge of HDFC co-ops is exactly the expertise needed at BSA.
chapters.title: Public: Arielle Hirsch (UHAB) supports Mangin, citing community education work

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: Thanks, Chair Ung and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: My name is Arielle Hirsch, and I'm the Director of Policy at UHAB.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: For 50 years, UHAB has empowered low- to moderate-income residents to take control of their housing and become homeowners in the buildings where they already live.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: We turn distressed rental housing into lasting, affordable co-ops, provide comprehensive training and technical assistance to keep these homes healthy and stable in the long term, and we would offer our support for the nomination of John Mangin to the chair of

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: board, sorry, to the Board of Standards and Appeals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: The majority of our work does not concern land use policy, but obviously in affordable housing, so many of these things are interconnected.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: We'll submit written testimony, but I don't get to be the first person to bring this prop today, but I am bringing it because it still lives in our office, and this series on what is affordable housing, zoning, and ULERP,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: which John Mangin helped to create and draft in his time at COP, the Center for Urban Pedagogy, has helped us to educate

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: many decades now of community members and homeowners and understanding their rights and obligations around their land use and housing policy and how to engage in their local community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: I cannot personally think of somebody who is more qualified to engage with community in a thoughtful and considerate and respectful way, having done so much legwork in our city to help folks not only understand

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: their rights and responsibilities, but also how to engage with those structures of power and to be able to shape and change them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: I'll also note that it is really important to have someone who is a technical expert.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: I'm glad to go after Brad because I don't have the technical expertise, but I noticed in the testimony earlier, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: Manjan mentioned some of the particularities of HDFC co-ops when they come through some of these appeals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: These are the kinds of nitty-gritty technical specifics that are really useful to have in a chair, and we strongly support his nomination.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Arielle Hirsch
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Thank you both for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: You're now excused.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Okay, nobody else?

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Yep, I could join.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Great.

chapters.summary: Seeing no further public speakers, Ung closes the public hearing, thanks candidates, committee members, staff, and the public for their participation, and adjourns the Committee on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards and Ethics.
chapters.title: Chair Ung closes hearing and adjourns committee

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Seeing no other members of the public sound to speak, this public hearing is now closed.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: I'd like to thank the candidates, the member of the committee, committee staff, the sergeant at arms, the member of public for their participation in today's meeting.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: The meeting of the Committee on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards, and Ethics is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Thank you.

summary: The Committee on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards and Ethics held a confirmation hearing on three mayoral nominees: Lisa Garcia for the NYC Land Bank Board of Directors, Dr. Dave Chokshi for the Board of Health, and John Mangin as Chair of the Board of Standards and Appeals.
Garcia and Chokshi faced relatively brief Q&A on land bank operations, public health equity, vaccination, and COVID-era policies; both nominees were excused without controversy.

Mangin's nomination dominated the hearing with extensive questioning from multiple council members about his academic writings on exclusionary zoning, the 2025 Charter Revision Commission that reduced council land use powers, community benefits agreements, and his commitment to transparency and local input at BSA; public testimony was overwhelmingly supportive.
